content.text:
The drawing shows a 5-methoxyindole with a 3-CH=N-NH-C(=N-pentyl)NH2 side chain (an aminoguanidine hydrazone).

**Indole core:** The pyrrole NH is at the top, bonded to C2, which connects to C3. C3 carries the CH= substituent. The benzene ring runs C3a, C4, C5 (bearing OMe), C6, C7, C7a. In the drawing, C3a is at (1024, 763) and C4 at (1097, 890). C5 at (1244, 890) bears the OMe, so the methoxy is at position 5.

**Side chain:** C3 is bonded to CH=N, then N-H, then the central carbon. That carbon is bonded to NH2 and to =N-nPent, with the pentyl written as an n-pentyl chain (CCCCC).

**Stereochemistry:** The hydrazone C=N geometry is drawn, so I assigned it. The C3 attachment at (880, 733) sits on the CH at (770, 830). The CH=N double bond runs to N at (630, 790), and that N bonds to NH at (520, 880).

Taking the CH=N bond, the CH carbon has the indole substituent at the upper left (880, 733). The N has its NH substituent at the lower left (520, 880). Relative to the double bond axis, the indole is on the upper side and the NH is on the lower side, so they are on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES for the side chain: c1(/C=N/NC(N)=NCCCCC)c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

Checking the direction: with `/C=N/N`, the indole before the C is written as "c1(/C=N/N...)", meaning the bond from the aromatic carbon to C is "/" and the bond from N to N is "/". This gives the trans arrangement, which is E.

SMILES: CCCCCN=C(N)N/N=C/c1c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12
